question.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=-\frac{1}{4}{t}^{2},\,y=-\frac{1}{6}t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =-4x,\,t=-6y.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =36{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=-4x$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}36{y}^{2} & =-4x \\ {y}^{2} & =-\frac{1}{9}x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian equation of the parabola is ${y}^{2}=-\frac{1}{9}x.$
